name: Ferrogate CL-9 L-Train
description: The arterial rail system of GLMZ, running elevated tracks through every district above Tier 2. The CL-9 cars are sixty years old and it shows — rattling frames, flickering displays, seats worn to bare metal. But it runs. Twenty hours a day, every eleven minutes, packed to capacity and beyond. For most of the city, the L is the only way to get anywhere that walking can't reach. The smell is a signature blend of ozone, sweat, and cheap synth-coffee.
propulsion: Electromagnetic rail, third-rail power draw from Meridian grid
speed: Average 45 km/h, peak 80 km/h between stations
range: Full loop: 94 km circuit through 47 stations
cost: Φ2 per ride, Φ45 monthly pass
autonomy: Automated with manual override capability. Ferrogate dispatch controls routing.
common_usage: Daily commute for millions. The lifeblood of the working class. Students, laborers, gig workers, and anyone who can't afford better.
story_hooks: L-train breakdowns strand thousands and create temporary communities on platforms
Certain late-night cars are known to run routes that aren't on any schedule — ghost trains to stations that don't exist on the map
physical_description: The CL-9 is a corroded steel tube on wheels, its once-white exterior now streaked with rust-orange and industrial grime, graffiti layered beneath decades of failed cleaning attempts. Interior walls are scarred aluminum, their synthetic panels peeling to expose wiring and structural ribs; overhead rails are pitted and discolored, casting hard shadows across rows of metal seats bolted to the floor. Windows are reinforced polycarbonate, clouded and scratched, with emergency route maps barely legible beneath condensation and fingerprints.
